post.caption: Ruby was named for a birthstone. In 1987, Larry Wall released Perl, first called Pearl. Another language already had that name, so he dropped the a. In Japan, Yukihiro Matsumoto wanted a jewel name for his new language. On February 24, 1993, he settled the name in an online chat. The choices were Coral and Ruby. Ruby won, and a colleague's birthstone was ruby. Later he noticed pearl is June's birthstone and ruby is July's. Printers' pearl type is 5 points, and their ruby type is 5.5. Ruby's packaged libraries are called gems.
